description: How the world map of money flipped: China’s meteoric rise vs the stagnation of old powers. Annual nominal GDP (current US$) for the top five economies, 2006–2026 (IMF/WB historical + near-term estimates). Watch China explode upward, India climb, and legacy exporters struggle after shocks (2008, 2013 yen volatility, COVID-19).
youtube_description:
The GDP Power Shift — ANIMATED (2006–2026)

Watch 21 years of global economic history compress into 90 seconds: China’s industrial surge, the US’s steady lead, Japan and Germany’s struggles, and India’s steady climb. This chart-race uses nominal GDP in current US$ (billions) — real-world data from IMF and World Bank (historical + short-term estimates). Key story beats: China’s explosive expansion after WTO-era growth, the 2008 global shock, COVID-19 dips in 2020, the stimulus-fueled US rebound, and India emerging as a fast riser.

Like, share, and subscribe for more visual economic stories. Tell us which takeover surprised you most in the comments — and suggest the next race we should animate.

Sources: IMF World Economic Outlook, World Bank (nominal GDP, current US$), national statistics agencies (compiled). Links in pinned comment.
